hints: Start from atomic numbers, Na is 11 and Mg is 12, and think what that tells you about electrons, orbitals and neutrons.
Work out neutrons with neutrons = mass number minus proton number, you will get 12 for both atoms.
Compare their full electron configurations and remember that metals that lose electrons easily act as electron donors.
walkthrough:
**Find protons and electrons**

Both are neutral atoms, so protons = electrons = atomic number.

$$^{23}\text{Na}: p = 11, e = 11 \quad \text{and} \quad ^{24}\text{Mg}: p = 12, e = 12$$

**Test statement 1 - filled orbitals**

Write the configurations and count only fully filled orbitals.

$$\text{Na}: 1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^1 \quad \text{and} \quad \text{Mg}: 1s^2 2s^2 2p^6 3s^2$$
Na has 5 filled orbitals (1s, 2s, three 2p), Mg has 6 filled orbitals (the same five plus 3s). So statement 1 is incorrect.

**Test statement 2 - neutrons**

Use the simple rule, neutrons = nucleon number minus proton number.

$$\text{Na}: 23 - 11 = 12 \quad \text{and} \quad \text{Mg}: 24 - 12 = 12$$
Both have 12 neutrons, so they are isotones. So statement 2 is correct.

**Test statement 3 - reducing agents**

A reducing agent loses (donates) electrons and is itself oxidised. Both Na and Mg are reactive Group 1 and Group 2 metals that readily form $\text{Na}^+$ and $\text{Mg}^{2+}$.

$$\text{Na} \rightarrow \text{Na}^+ + e^- \quad \text{and} \quad \text{Mg} \rightarrow \text{Mg}^{2+} + 2e^-$$
So statement 3 is correct.

**Combine the verdict**

Statement 1 is false, statements 2 and 3 are true. That combination matches the 2 and 3 only option.

options.A: Incorrect because this means 1, 2 and 3 are all correct. Statement 1 fails since Na has an unpaired half-filled 3s orbital while Mg has a filled 3s orbital.
options.B: Incorrect because this means 1 and 2 only are correct. Statement 1 is false and statement 3 is true, so this combination cannot be right.
options.C: Correct because this means 2 and 3 only are correct. Both have 12 neutrons and both metals readily lose electrons, so both act as reducing agents.
options.D: Incorrect because this means 1 only is correct. Statement 1 is the one false statement, while 2 and 3 are both true.
